brief.headline: Qualify a second converter and line up film-maker benchmarks — Silk Polypack publishes no financials, so we lean on our ₹7775 spend and three credible alternates to push payment from 30 to 15 days, freeing up ₹320 for us.

priceAsk.summary: Hold the line at the current price; focus this round on payment terms and qualifying a backup.
priceAsk.basis: Our current laminate price sits at the top of the fair band (₹205–305/kg market ask, typical ₹250/kg), so there's little room to squeeze further right now. The import benchmark for BOPET film is 171.60 ₹/kg, meaning conversion and specialty layers add roughly ₹80/kg — reasonable for pharma-grade sachet laminate. Push price only if a second converter quotes materially lower.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Ask to cut payment from 30 days after receipt to 15 days after receipt.
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: ₹320 cash freed up for us if we move to 15 days sooner (₹639 total freed at 30 days faster, ₹320 for the extra 15-day step).

brief.financialLeverage: Silk Polypack is a private firm that does not publish financials, so we have no window into their revenue, profit, or how tight their cash is. That means we build our leverage from what we do know: we spend ₹7775 a year with them, and we have at least three strong alternate converters — Huhtamaki India Ltd (₹2755.75 Cr revenue), UFLEX Ltd (₹16492.00 Cr), and Constantia Parikh Packaging Pvt Ltd (₹222.04 Cr) — all of whom can handle pharma laminate sachets at scale. Because we can't see their books, the safest play is to line up a qualified second source now and use that credibly to ask for faster payment; if they resist, we have a clear path to split the volume.

alternates.name: Huhtamaki India Ltd
alternates.why: Listed flexible-packaging converter (₹2755.75 Cr revenue, already a tiny FDC supplier) — a proven, scalable second source for laminate sachets.

alternates.name: UFLEX Ltd
alternates.why: Listed flexibles giant (₹16492.00 Cr revenue) — both film substrate AND conversion; can second-source at scale.

alternates.name: Constantia Parikh Packaging Pvt Ltd
alternates.why: Global Constantia group's India converter (₹222.04 Cr revenue) — pharma blister/sachet laminates; strong second-source fit.

risks: Silk Polypack publishes no financials — we cannot judge their cash position or stability, so push firmly but avoid a squeeze that could break a fragile supplier.
Our ₹7775 spend is very small; they may not prioritize us if we push too hard without a credible plan to grow volume or split it elsewhere.
The market ask verdict is 'MARKET-FAIR (top of fair band)' — our price is already at the high end of reasonable, so a big price cut is unlikely unless a second converter undercuts them.

We have strong listed alternates (Huhtamaki, UFLEX) and leads on film-makers (Polyplex, Ester, Jindal, Garware, SRF) and another converter (Constantia), but none are qualified yet — start those RFQs now so the threat is real in 60 days.
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We'd like to tighten payment to 15 days after receipt to free up working cash on our side, and in parallel we're qualifying a second laminate converter — can you work with us on faster terms to keep this a single-source partnership?
